missions.fullAnalysis: Strategic focus: Nominative subject. 'Пост' stays in the nominative as the subject of 'стоит'. 'Охранный' is the agreeing masculine adjective, and 'на углу' gives the location.
Strategic focus: Accusative object. 'Пост' is the accusative direct object of 'занял'; for this inanimate masculine noun the accusative matches the nominative. 'Свой' marks it as his own post.
Strategic focus: Genitive of absence. 'Поста' takes the genitive after 'нет' to express what is missing. 'Полицейского' agrees in the masculine genitive, and 'у моста' sets the place.
Strategic focus: Dative after к. 'Посту' is in the dative case after 'к', marking the goal of motion. 'Офицер' is the nominative subject of 'подошёл'.
Strategic focus: Instrumental after за. 'Постом' takes the instrumental case after 'за' to show position beyond. 'Граница' is the nominative subject of 'начинается'.
Strategic focus: Prepositional after на. 'Посту' uses the special stressed 'у' ending in the prepositional after 'на' to mark location. 'Солдат' is the nominative subject.
Strategic focus: Accusative after на with motion. 'Пост' is accusative after 'на' because there is movement back to it. 'Вечером' is instrumental, giving the time.
Strategic focus: Nominative plural subject. 'Посты' is the nominative plural subject of 'стоят'. 'Военные' agrees in the plural, and 'вдоль дороги' uses the genitive.
Strategic focus: Genitive plural after несколько. 'Постов' takes the genitive plural after 'несколько'. 'Проверочных' agrees in the genitive plural, naming the checkpoints.
Strategic focus: Nominative subject with accusative object. 'Пост' is the nominative subject of 'охраняет', and 'мост' is its accusative object. 'Этот' agrees in the masculine.
